1.name: Control wheel
1.spec: Ram's-horn yoke, one per front seat
1.note: Turn it for the ailerons, push or pull it for the elevator. About 80° of turn each way and 113 mm of pull to the stops.

2.name: Control column tube
2.note: Slides fore and aft through the panel and turns with the wheel. Its splines drive the sprocket shaft, so turning and sliding never fight each other.

3.name: Column bearing
3.note: Carries the column where it passes the panel, letting it slide and turn with little friction and no play.

4.name: Sprocket
4.spec: 12 teeth, 3/8 in pitch, Ø36.8 pitch circle
4.note: Turns the wheel's rotation into chain travel: 18.4 mm of cable per radian, so full wheel moves the aileron cables 25.8 mm.

5.name: Roller chain
5.note: Wraps over the sprocket; one end rises as the other falls. Cables are swaged to both ends, so the chain is the loop's only bend that has to grip.

6.name: Aileron cables
6.spec: Ø3.2 7×19, four runs in one loop
6.note: One closed loop: left wing, the interconnect between the two wheels, right wing, and the balance cable from wingtip to wingtip. Pull one end, the other pays out.

7.name: Pulley
7.note: Turns a cable round a corner. Its diameter is about 24 times the cable's, so the wires bend gently and last.

8.name: Pulley bracket and guard pins
8.spec: Two plates, AN3 bolt, two pins
8.note: Holds the pulley to the structure. The guard pins sit closer to the flange than half a cable's width, so a slack cable cannot jump off the groove.

9.name: Fairlead
9.spec: Split, at each bulkhead and wing root
9.note: A smooth guide where a cable passes a bulkhead: it stops the cable rubbing through the frame. A cable may bend no more than 3° in one.

10.name: Turnbuckle
10.note: Right-hand thread one end, left-hand the other: turning the barrel draws both cable ends in and sets the rigging tension, then the clips lock it.

11.name: Aileron bellcrank
11.note: In each wing: the cable loop pulls its two arms, its third arm pushes the rod. Its stops end the travel, so the wheel can't overdrive the aileron.

12.name: Aileron push-pull rod
12.note: Runs aft from the bellcrank through the rear spar to the aileron's horn, the same 13.8 mm forward or back at full wheel.

13.name: Aileron with horn
13.note: Its horn leans 36.8° forward, so equal rod travel lifts it 20° but lowers it only 15°: less drag on the rising wing, less adverse yaw.

14.name: Elevator push tube
14.spec: Collar on the column to the idler
14.note: Carries the column's fore-and-aft travel to the idler, one per seat, so both wheels always move the elevator together.

15.name: Elevator idler
15.note: A bellcrank across the cabin: the push tubes turn it, its short arms pull the up and down cables 0.4 mm for each millimetre of column.

16.name: Elevator cables
16.note: Under the floor and up the tail cone. Pulling the column pulls the up cable; the air load shows as one cable tighter than the other.

17.name: Elevator bellcrank
17.note: Bolted to the elevator's torque tube: the up cable on its upper arm, the down cable on its lower one, so each cable only ever pulls.

18.name: Stop bolts
18.note: Screwed into a frame where the bellcrank lands at 28° up and 23° down. Adjustable, then locked: they, not the pilot, set the travel.

19.name: Elevator
19.spec: Two halves on one torque tube, 1.06 m²
19.note: Sets the tail's lift and so the angle of attack. The air pushes it back toward neutral; that hinge moment is what the pilot holds.

20.name: Rudder pedals
20.note: Push the right pedal and the right pedals go forward, the left ones come back: 102 mm of toe travel gives 17° of rudder.

21.name: Rudder cables
21.note: From each pedal tube's arm, along the floor and up the tail cone to the horn. Left pedal pulls the left cable, right pedal the right.

22.name: Rudder horn
22.note: Turns the cables' pull into rudder angle: 36.5 mm of cable at the horn swings the rudder its full 17°.

23.name: Rudder
23.note: Yaws the nose. In a turn it is used to cancel the aileron's adverse yaw, about a third of the aileron's angle in this aeroplane.

24.name: Steering bungee
24.spec: Spring link to the nose gear
24.note: Lets the pedals steer the nose wheel ±10° on the ground. In the air the gear's cams hold the wheel straight and the bungee just stretches.

25.name: Trim wheel and drum
25.note: Roll the top aft for nose up. About six turns cover the whole tab travel: fine enough to set the stick force to nothing.

26.name: Trim cables
26.note: Wound on the trim wheel's drum and on the actuator's drum at the tail; they reach the elevator along its hinge line, so pitch doesn't pull them.

27.name: Trim tab actuator
27.note: The cable turns its drum and screw; the nut moves 2 mm a turn. A lead of 4° under a friction angle of 8.5° locks it: the air can't wind it back.

28.name: Trim push-pull rod
28.note: Pushes or pulls the tab's horn as the nut runs. It leaves the elevator through its lower skin, so the horn sits outside in the airflow.

29.name: Trim tab
29.note: A small flap on the elevator's edge. Set down, the air pushes it up, and that moment holds the elevator up for the pilot: stick force to zero.
